body:
# Story: Bump Minimum Python Version to 3.11

## Rationale
Currently, our codebase supports Python 3.9+. However, observing the Python ecosystem in 2025/2026:
- **Python 3.9** reached End-of-Life (EOL) in October 2025 and no longer receives security updates.
- **Python 3.10** is the oldest supported branch and will reach EOL in October 2026.
- The majority of the active Python ecosystem (over 70%) has migrated to Python 3.11, 3.12, or 3.13.

By bumping our minimum supported version to **Python 3.11**:
1. **Performance Improvements:** We can take full advantage of the "Faster CPython" initiative introduced in 3.11 (yielding 10-60% faster execution without code changes).
2. **Modern Syntax and Standard Library:** We gain full access to `match/case` (introduced in 3.10), native `asyncio` task groups, `ExceptionGroup`, and dramatically better error tracebacks.
3. **Reduced Maintenance:** We can remove numerous legacy backward-compatibility shims inside `_compat.py` and `typing_extensions` fallbacks.
4. **Security:** We proactively push our users toward actively supported, secure Python environments.

*(Note: Our Docker images are already built on `python:3.11` and `python:3.11-slim`, meaning production deployments are partially isolated from this bump, primarily affecting local developers and script consumers.)*

---

## Execution Plan

An evaluation of the codebase has been conducted to ensure a complete migration. The following steps must be executed to fulfill this story:

### 1. Update Project Metadata
- [ ] **`pyproject.toml`**: 
  - Change `requires-python = ">=3.9"` to `>=3.11`.
  - Update `classifiers` (remove `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.9` and `3.10`).
  - Update `tool.ruff.target-version` from `"py39"` to `"py311"`.
  - Update `tool.mypy.python_version` from `"3.9"` to `"3.11"`.

### 2. Update Continuous Integration (CI)
- [ ] **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: Ensure the test matrix excludes `3.9` (update `python-version: ["3.9", "3.12"]` to `["3.11", "3.12"]`).
- [ ] **`.github/workflows/ci-full.yml`**: Remove `3.9` and `3.10` from the comprehensive matrix `["3.9", "3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]`.

### 3. Clean Up Compatibility Code
- [ ] **`src/file_organizer/_compat.py`**: Remove specific Python `3.9` and `3.10` compatibility shims (e.g., polyfills for `datetime.timezone.utc`, `typing` fallbacks like `GenericAlias` and `Optional` backward support).
- [ ] **`src/` codebase wide**: Remove `# noqa: UP035 — required for Typer on Python 3.9` from CLI modules (`daemon.py`, `main.py`, `rules.py`, `dedupe_v2.py`, etc.). Remove any usage of `typing_extensions` where the standard `typing` module in 3.11 now suffices.

### 4. Update Documentation
- [ ] **`README.md`** & **`docs/`**: Search and replace any mention of "Python 3.9+" with "Python 3.11+".
- [ ] **`file_organizer_v2/site/getting-started/index.html`** (and source markdown): Update system requirements indicating the new minimal version.
- [ ] **`project-docs/claude/TASK_REVIEW_*.md`**: Update context notes stating "Python 3.9+" to reflect the new baseline.

## Verification Checklist

- [ ] **Packaging Metadata**: Verify `pyproject.toml` correctly requires Python >= 3.11 and the PyPI classifiers are updated.
- [ ] **Type Checker / Linters**: Verify `mypy` and `ruff` are configured for Python 3.11 target, passing all checks after removing backwards compat code.
- [ ] **Continuous Integration (CI)**: Verify GitHub actions matrix jobs complete successfully exclusively on Python 3.11+.
- [ ] **Local Install**: Verify that installing the project locally (`pip install -e .`) succeeds on Python 3.11+.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: Ensure all unit tests pass locally using `pytest` specifically on Python 3.11 or greater.
- [ ] **Docker**: Validate Docker images build appropriately and the application starts securely via `docker-compose up`.
title: Bump Minimum Python Version to 3.11

body:
## Parent

Sub-issue of #369 ([Enhancement] Add `act` for full local CI simulation via Docker)

## Why

File Organizer ships on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Our CI currently runs **only** on `ubuntu-latest`. Windows-specific code paths are untested in CI:

- `os.name == 'nt'` branches — path separator logic, registry access
- `os.stat().st_ctime` — on Windows this IS creation time (unlike Linux where it's inode change time)
- `build_windows.ps1` / `build_windows.iss` — Windows build scripts never validated in CI
- Path separators (`\` vs `/`) — many file operations assume POSIX paths
- `pathlib.PureWindowsPath` vs `PurePosixPath` edge cases
- Long path support (`MAX_PATH` 260 character limit)
- File locking behaviour — Windows locks open files differently than Linux/macOS

## What

Add a `windows-latest` runner to `ci-full.yml` with a **cost-conscious** configuration:

```yaml
  test-windows:
    name: Test Windows (Python 3.12)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    # Only run on main push + weekly schedule (not every PR)
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install -e ".[dev]"
      - run: pytest tests/ -m "not regression" --override-ini="addopts="
```

### Cost Analysis

| Runner | Per-minute rate | Estimated run | Cost per run |
|--------|----------------|---------------|-------------|
| ubuntu-latest | $0.008 | ~5 min | ~$0.04 |
| **windows-latest** | **$0.016** | ~8 min | **~$0.13** |

Windows runners cost **2x** Linux (much cheaper than macOS at 10x). Still cost-control:
- Run only on `push` to `main` (not on every PR)
- Add weekly schedule as a safety net
- Test **only Python 3.12** on Windows (not the full 3.9–3.12 matrix)

### Trigger Strategy

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'  # Weekly Monday 06:00 UTC
```

## Windows Developer Experience (WSL2)

Windows contributors can use WSL2 + `act` (#369) to get Linux CI parity locally:

```bash
# In WSL2 terminal
wsl
brew install act    # or install via curl
act pull_request    # runs ci-full.yml in Docker
```

This covers the Linux CI matrix. The Windows-native runner catches Windows-specific issues
that WSL2 cannot (real Windows paths, file locking, registry).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test-windows` job added to `ci-full.yml`
- [ ] Job runs on `windows-latest` with Python 3.12
- [ ] Job triggers only on `main` push + weekly schedule
- [ ] Job does NOT trigger on PRs (cost control)
- [ ] All existing tests pass on Windows runner (or failures documented)
- [ ] Windows-specific test failures triaged and fixed or skipped with markers
- [ ] `CONTRIBUTING.md` updated with WSL2 + `act` instructions for Windows devs

## Known Issues to Expect

Tests likely to fail on Windows (requiring platform-aware fixes or skip markers):

1. **Path separator tests** — hardcoded `/` in assertions
2. **Symlink tests** — Windows requires elevated privileges for symlinks
3. **File permission tests** — Windows ACL model differs from POSIX
4. **Temp directory paths** — `C:\Users\...` vs `/tmp/...`

## Out of Scope

- Full Python matrix on Windows (not cost-effective)
- Windows installer validation (separate build story)
- Windows ARM64 runner (not available on GitHub Actions)

## Priority

**Low** — 2x cost makes this more feasible than macOS (10x), but local WSL2 + `act` covers most cases. This is a CI safety net.

## Related

- #369 — `act` for local CI simulation (parent)
- #370 — macOS CI runner (sibling sub-issue)
- #367 — Local test matrix script
- `scripts/build_windows.ps1` — Windows build script
- `scripts/build_windows.iss` — InnoSetup installer config
title: [CI] Add Windows runner to GitHub Actions test matrix

## Parent

Sub-issue of #369 ([Enhancement] Add `act` for full local CI simulation via Docker)

## Why

File Organizer ships on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Our CI currently runs **only** on `ubuntu-latest`. macOS-specific code paths are untested in CI:

- `os.stat().st_birthtime` — macOS-only attribute (caused #101)
- `DeviceType.MPS` / `DeviceType.METAL` — Apple Silicon GPU detection
- `build_macos.sh` — macOS build script never validated in CI
- Framework paths (`/Library/Frameworks/`, Homebrew paths) — differ from Linux
- File system case sensitivity — macOS is case-insensitive by default

## What

Add a `macos-latest` runner to `ci-full.yml` with a **cost-conscious** configuration:

```yaml
  test-macos:
    name: Test macOS (Python 3.12)
    runs-on: macos-latest
    # Only run on main push + weekly schedule (not every PR)
    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pip install -e ".[dev]"
      - run: pytest tests/ -m "not regression" --override-ini="addopts="
```

### Cost Analysis

| Runner | Per-minute rate | Estimated run | Cost per run |
|--------|----------------|---------------|-------------|
| ubuntu-latest | $0.008 | ~5 min | ~$0.04 |
| **macos-latest** | **$0.08** | ~5 min | **~$0.40** |

macOS runners cost **10x** Linux. To control costs:
- Run only on `push` to `main` (not on every PR)
- Add weekly schedule as a safety net
- Test **only Python 3.12** on macOS (not the full 3.9–3.12 matrix)

### Trigger Strategy

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:

```

- [ ] Job triggers only on `main` push + weekly schedule
- [ ] Job does NOT trigger on PRs (cost control)

body:
## Overview

[`act`](https://github.com/nektos/act) runs GitHub Actions workflows locally inside Docker containers that mirror `ubuntu-latest`. This is the upgrade path from the shell-based `scripts/test-local-matrix.sh` (implemented in #367) to full CI parity — including OS-level matching.

## Why

`scripts/test-local-matrix.sh` (#367) covers the Python version matrix and frontend tests, but runs on the **host OS** (macOS/Windows). This means platform-specific bugs (e.g., `st_birthtime` on macOS vs `st_mtime` on Linux) are still invisible locally.

`act` solves this by running the actual `.github/workflows/*.yml` files inside ubuntu-latest Docker containers — identical to what GitHub Actions does.

## What

### Installation

```bash
# macOS
brew install act

# Linux
curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nektos/act/master/install.sh | sudo bash

# Windows
choco install act-cli
```

### Usage

```bash
# Run the full ci-full.yml matrix (simulates a PR)
act pull_request

# Run just the Python test matrix
act pull_request -j test-matrix

# Run just the frontend job
act pull_request -j frontend-compat

# Run the fast CI (ci.yml push to main)
act push
```

### Project Configuration (`.actrc`)

Create a `.actrc` file in the project root:

```
-P ubuntu-latest=ghcr.io/catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest
--container-architecture linux/amd64
```

This pins the Docker image to match GitHub's actual ubuntu-latest runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.actrc` added to project root with correct image configuration
- [ ] `act` usage documented in `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- [ ] Verified: `act pull_request` reproduces CI failures locally
- [ ] Verified: `act pull_request -j test-matrix` runs Python 3.9/3.10/3.11/3.12
- [ ] Verified: `act pull_request -j frontend-compat` runs Node 18.x frontend tests

## Prerequisites

- Docker Desktop running locally
- ~2 GB disk for ubuntu-latest Docker image (first run)

## Trade-offs

| | `act` (this issue) | `test-local-matrix.sh` (#367) |
|--|-----|------|
| OS parity | ✅ ubuntu-latest in Docker | ❌ Host OS (macOS/Windows) |
| Workflow sync | ✅ Uses actual YAML — stays in sync automatically | ⚠️ Must be updated manually when CI changes |
| Speed | Slower (Docker overhead) | Faster (native execution) |
| Dependencies | Docker Desktop required | pyenv only |
| Offline | ❌ Needs Docker images cached | ✅ Works fully offline |

## Relationship to Other Issues

- **Parent of**: macOS CI runner story, Windows CI runner story
- **Extends**: #367 (local test parity — shell script approach)
- **Related**: #331 (E2E tests disabled)

**Acknowledged as a known limitation of the current Phase 1 implementation.** The in-process metadata import is an intentional trade-off documented in the module docstring: plugins are imported once in-process for metadata/dependency validation, then all subsequent lifecycle calls run through the subprocess executor. A fully hardened system would extract metadata via a static manifest (e.g., `plugin.json`) or a separate sandboxed subprocess. That work is deferred to a follow-on hardening task as it requires a significant architectural change (and all plugin authors would need to add a manifest file). The current design is a meaningful improvement over pre-PR behavior (zero isolation) while keeping the scope manageable.

## Summary

The Playwright E2E test suite consistently fails in the \`frontend-test\` CI job with:

\`\`\`
Error: Process from config.webServer exited early.
\`\`\`

This is a pre-existing failure present on the \`epic/phase-6-web-interface\` branch. The job is currently configured with \`continue-on-error: true\` to avoid blocking CI, but the underlying problem should be fixed.

## Root Cause

The \`playwright.config.js\` \`webServer\` option attempts to start the full application backend before running E2E tests. In CI, the backend dependencies (Ollama, Redis, Celery, database) are not available, so the server process exits immediately and Playwright aborts all tests before any run.

## Evidence

From CI run [22106010135](https://github.com/curdriceaurora/Local-File-Organizer/actions/runs/22106010135):

\`\`\`
Run E2E tests
Error: Process from config.webServer exited early.
Process completed with exit code 1.
\`\`\`

Affected jobs: \`frontend-test (18.x)\` and \`frontend-test (20.x)\`

## Current Workaround

\`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` has \`continue-on-error: true\` on the \`Run E2E tests\` step, so CI remains green overall.

## Proposed Fix Options

1. **Mock/stub the webServer** — Create a lightweight static server or mock API server that satisfies Playwright's \`webServer\` check without requiring Ollama/Redis/Celery
2. **Separate E2E from unit tests** — Move E2E tests to a separate workflow that only runs on \`main\` pushes (not PRs) or requires manual trigger, where a real environment could be spun up
3. **Use Playwright's \`use.baseURL\` without webServer** — Skip the \`webServer\` config and use environment variables for the base URL; skip E2E tests entirely if \`SKIP_E2E=true\`
4. **Docker Compose in CI** — Add a \`docker-compose.test.yml\` to spin up the full stack in CI for E2E runs

## Files Involved

- \`playwright.config.js\` — \`webServer\` configuration
- \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` — \`frontend-test\` job, \`Run E2E tests\` step

## CCPM Tracking

**Epic**: phase-6-web-interface
**Priority**: Medium
**Effort Estimate**: 2-4 hours
**Status**: Backlog

## Related

- CI run: https://github.com/curdriceaurora/Local-File-Organizer/actions/runs/22106010135
- Component tests (Jest/jsdom): ✅ passing — only E2E (Playwright) is affected
title: [Bug] Playwright E2E tests fail in CI: webServer exits early (no backend available)

# Task 003: Build audio content-based organization

## Description

Implement intelligent content-based organization for audio files using both transcribed content and metadata. This task creates smart categorization to distinguish between music, podcasts, recordings, and other audio types, then organizes them into logical folder structures based on their content and characteristics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Automatically categorize audio files by type (music, podcast, recording, audiobook, etc.)
- [ ] Organize music files by artist, album, and genre
- [ ] Organize podcasts by show name, episode number, and date
- [ ] Organize voice recordings by date, topic, and speakers
- [ ] Create folder structure automatically based on audio type
- [ ] Use transcribed content for topic-based organization
- [ ] Support custom organization rules and templates
- [ ] Handle duplicate detection and consolidation
- [ ] Provide organization preview before moving files
- [ ] Generate organization reports with statistics
- [ ] Support batch organization with progress tracking
- [ ] Integration tests with complete organization workflows

## Technical Details

### Implementation Approach

1. **Audio Type Classification**
   - Analyze metadata patterns to determine type
   - Use transcription content for context
   - Machine learning classifier for ambiguous cases
   - Rule-based classification for clear patterns

   **Classification Rules:**
   - **Music**: Has artist/album tags, short tracks (<10 min), no speech
   - **Podcast**: Episode metadata, 15-90 min duration, conversational speech
   - **Audiobook**: Chapter metadata, long duration (>30 min), narrative speech
   - **Voice Recording**: No metadata, variable length, often meeting/memo keywords
   - **Interview**: Multiple speakers, Q&A pattern in transcription

2. **Organization Strategies**

   **Music Organization:**
   ```
   Music/
   ├── {Genre}/
   │   └── {Artist}/
   │       └── {Album}/
   │           └── {TrackNum} - {Title}.{ext}
   ```

   **Podcast Organization:**
   ```
   Podcasts/
   ├── {Show Name}/
   │   └── {Year}/
   │       └── {Episode} - {Title} ({Date}).{ext}
   ```

   **Recording Organization:**
   ```
   Recordings/
   ├── {Year}/
   │   └── {Month}/
   │       └── {Topic or Keywords}/
   │           └── {Date} - {Description}.{ext}
   ```

3. **Content Analysis Integration**
   - Use transcription to extract topics and keywords
   - Apply NLP for topic modeling
   - Extract dates and event names from speech
   - Identify speaker names for attribution

4. **Smart Folder Creation**
   - Generate folder names from metadata
   - Sanitize names for filesystem compatibility
   - Handle naming conflicts automatically
   - Maintain consistent naming conventions

5. **Duplicate Detection**
   - Compare audio fingerprints
   - Check metadata similarity
   - Identify re-encoded versions
   - Merge or flag duplicates

### File Structure
```
file_organizer_v2/src/file_organizer/
├── services/
│   ├── audio_classifier.py       # Type classification
│   ├── audio_organizer.py        # Main organization logic
│   └── audio_duplicate_detector.py  # Duplicate detection
├── core/
│   └── organization_rules.py     # Rule engine
└── utils/
    └── path_utils.py              # Path sanitization
```

### Key Classes

```python
class AudioClassifier:
    """Classify audio files by type"""

    def classify(
        self,
        metadata: AudioMetadata,
        transcription: Optional[TranscriptionResult] = None
    ) -> AudioType:
        """Determine audio file type"""

    def get_classification_confidence(self) -> float:
        """Return confidence score for classification"""


class AudioOrganizer:
    """Organize audio files based on content and metadata"""

    def __init__(self, rules: OrganizationRules):
        """Initialize with organization rules"""

    def preview_organization(
        self,
        files: List[str],
        base_path: str
    ) -> OrganizationPlan:
        """Preview how files will be organized"""

    def organize(
        self,
        files: List[str],
        base_path: str,
        dry_run: bool = True
    ) -> OrganizationResult:
        """Organize files according to rules"""

    def generate_path(
        self,
        audio_type: AudioType,
        metadata: AudioMetadata,
        transcription: Optional[TranscriptionResult] = None
    ) -> str:
        """Generate target path for audio file"""


class OrganizationRules:
    """Define organization rules and templates"""

    music_template: str = "{Genre}/{Artist}/{Album}/{TrackNum} - {Title}"
    podcast_template: str = "{Show}/{Year}/{Episode} - {Title}"
    recording_template: str = "Recordings/{Year}/{Month}/{Topic}/{Date}"

    def customize_template(self, audio_type: AudioType, template: str):
        """Set custom organization template"""
```

### Dependencies
- Task 001 (transcription) - required for content analysis
- Task 002 (metadata) - required for organization decisions
- librosa or audioflux (for audio fingerprinting)
- scikit-learn (for ML classification if needed)

### Performance Considerations
- Cache classification results
- Batch process multiple files
- Optimize path generation
- Parallelize duplicate detection
- Progress tracking for large batches

### User Experience
- Dry run mode to preview changes
- Confirmation prompts for large operations
- Detailed organization reports
- Undo/rollback capability
- Progress bars for batch operations

## Dependencies

- **Task 001**: Requires transcription functionality for content-based organization
- **Task 002**: Requires metadata extraction for classification and path generation

## Effort Estimate

**Size:** Medium (M)
**Estimated Hours:** 16 hours

### Breakdown:
- Audio type classification: 4 hours
- Organization rule engine: 3 hours
- Path generation and sanitization: 2 hours
- Content analysis integration: 3 hours
- Duplicate detection: 2 hours
- Testing and validation: 2 hours

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Code implemented and follows project style guidelines
- [ ] All acceptance criteria met
- [ ] Unit tests written and passing (>80% coverage)
- [ ] Integration tests with complete organization workflows
- [ ] Successfully classifies and organizes sample audio files
- [ ] Handles edge cases (missing metadata, corrupted files)
- [ ] Duplicate detection working accurately
- [ ] Dry run mode tested and functional
- [ ] Organization reports generated correctly
- [ ] Performance acceptable for large file sets (>1000 files)
- [ ] Code reviewed and approved
- [ ] Documentation with usage examples and templates
- [ ] No regression in existing functionality
- [ ] User-facing error messages clear and helpful

**Timeline:** Phase 2 & Phase 5  
**Status:** Planned

## Overview
Optimize processing speed, especially for image processing which currently takes ~4 minutes per image.

## Critical Issue 🚨
**Current State:**
- Text processing: ~7s per file ✅ (acceptable)
- **Image processing: ~240s (4 minutes) per file** ❌ (needs optimization)
- Target: <30s per image (8x improvement needed)

## Key Optimization Areas

### 1. Vision Model Optimization 🎯
Reduce image processing time
- **Model quantization** (explore lighter quantization)
- **Batch processing** (process multiple images together)
- **GPU acceleration** (CUDA/Metal support)
- **Model caching** (reduce loading time)
- **Alternative models** (explore faster models)
- **Inference optimization** (llama.cpp optimizations)

### 2. Text Model Optimization 📝
Maintain current speed or improve
- Model preloading
- Response caching for similar files
- Parallel processing support

### 3. Architecture Optimization 🏗️
System-level improvements
- **Async/await** for I/O operations
- **Multiprocessing** for CPU-bound tasks
- **Thread pooling** for model inference
- **Connection pooling** (Ollama)
- **Memory management** (reduce peak usage)

### 4. File I/O Optimization 💾
Faster file operations
- Streaming file reads
- Lazy loading
- Memory-mapped files
- Efficient image loading (PIL optimization)

### 5. Caching Strategy 🗄️
Avoid redundant processing
- File content hash-based cache
- Model response caching
- Metadata caching
- Cache invalidation strategy

### 6. Profiling & Monitoring 📊
Identify bottlenecks
- Performance profiling (cProfile, py-spy)
- Memory profiling
- Bottleneck identification
- Benchmark suite
- Continuous performance monitoring

## Performance Targets

| Component | Current | Phase 2 Target | Phase 5 Target |

# Epic: Feature Expansion (Phase 3)

**Timeline:** Weeks 5-7
**Status:** Planned
**Priority:** High

## Overview
Expand file type support and add advanced organization methodologies.

## Key Features

### 1. Audio File Support 🎵
Transcription and organization of audio files
- **Formats**: MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A, OGG
- Distil-Whisper integration for transcription
- Speaker identification
- Music metadata extraction (artist, album, genre)
- Language detection
- Organize by content/topic

### 2. Advanced Video Processing 🎥
Enhanced video analysis beyond first frame
- Multi-frame analysis (scene detection)
- Video transcription (audio track)
- Thumbnail generation
- Metadata extraction (resolution, duration, codec)
- Scene-based categorization

### 3. PARA Methodology 📂
Projects, Areas, Resources, Archive organization
- Automatic PARA categorization
- User-defined category rules
- Smart suggestions based on content
- Migration from flat structure
- PARA-aware folder generation

### 4. Johnny Decimal System 🔢
Hierarchical numbering for organization
- Auto-generate Johnny Decimal numbers
- User-defined numbering schemes
- Conflict resolution
- Documentation and guides
- Integration with existing structures

### 5. Enhanced Ebook Support 📚
Improved EPUB processing
- Chapter-based analysis
- Author and genre detection
- Series recognition
- Better metadata extraction

### 6. Format Expansion 📦
Additional file types
- CAD files (DWG, DXF)
- Archive files (ZIP, RAR, 7Z)
- Scientific data formats

## Success Criteria
- [ ] 20+ file types supported
- [ ] Audio transcription >90% accuracy
- [ ] PARA adoption by power users
- [ ] Video quality improved significantly
- [ ] Johnny Decimal implementation complete

## Technical Requirements
- faster-whisper 1.0+ (audio transcription)
- ffmpeg-python 0.2+ (video processing)
- Additional file format libraries

## Dependencies
- Phase 2 complete
- Audio model integration (Distil-Whisper)
